title: Update some field names to match what's in RFCs.
description:
Update some field names and capitalization in the IPv4, IPv6, ICMPv4,
and TCP dissectors to match the names documented in their respective
RFCs. This is in no way comprehensive, but it ensures that the packet
diagram more closely matches the RFC diagrams for those protocols.

(I haven't found a document that explitly says so, but protocol field
names in IETF RFCs seem to follow Chicago Manual of Style capitalization
recommendations in section 3.4 of the RFC Style Guide[1] for the most
part.)

[1]https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7322#section-3.4

notes.body: it is no Time To live ? (TTL)

This matches https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc791#section-3.1 and https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7322#section-3.4 ("Typically, all words in a title will be capitalized except for internal articles, prepositions, and conjunctions.") English would be easier if fewer people had invaded England over the past 2000 years. :smile:
it will not break some external tools check destination field ?
This is a bigger concern since this is a core protocol, but it passes our tests, and we do change field descriptions from time to time.
I don't mind doing so, but would this be more likely to break external tools?
Even if it does I think I prefere the header and the filter to match.
Not a fan of arbitrary renaming of filters unless there's a functional issue.
Is an alias possible so either `tcp.hdr_len` or `tcp.data_offset` work?

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/483/diffs?diff_id=116245435&start_sha=45854afcb93815c03736a0e5a42b5a82440cb679#ecc33d9ca259b01be33fa710cd6cf581a15d868b_6971_6973)

We have a similar issue in the IPv4 dissector -- it diverges slightly from RFC 791 by calling the "IHL" field "Header Length". I switched the name back to "Header Length" here and noted the divergence in a comment similar to packet-ip.c. We might be technically wrong in both cases, but at least we're *consistently* technically wrong.

The reason for the name mismatch is that the IPv4 "Header Length" field value is the computed length value, not the raw IHL value. They're different. So the newly added code comment ("IHL in the RFCs") is somewhat misleading IMO because it suggests it's just a naming difference.

Same logic applies to TCP.
